challenge.better_approach: Having the installer write the record would skip the tester, but the class's prove_gate names the tester and the store's door is the one seal path; the installer stays the apply side.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That clearance's standing() call is the only reader a host-seam proven_by meets; and that the short hostname lowercased is stable per box (bus/server.py:854 and groundloop/pulse.py:83 compare it the same way).
challenge.prior_art: installer.run_verify already runs the verify (reused as the method, not rebuilt); validation_store.persist_validation(artifact_path=...) seals human-proved artifacts by the artifact rule, which is the shape this extends with a per-box segment. Congruency lab: no host-seam seal intention exists.
challenge.real_collision: Q#90 (per-OS seals for code proofs) is a distinction, not a collision: one file per box per host-seam touches no code-seal record's shape or address.

answers.falsifier: Done: a fixture host-seam with verify `true` seals green and stands proven here; verify `false` seals red; a changed host fact, a record from another hostname, or an edited intention reads not proven. Wrong: clearance still cannot name the sealed intention as proof.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator measured it on tickets b1f182b6b818 and 496dcbeba174 (CairnCommons/tickets/): clearance.py refuses their crossing with "the crossing names no proof at all", since nothing seals a host-seam's verify, and node_classes/host-seam.json's prove_gate still reads "the tester (IOU: hand-run until built)"
answers.how: cairn test --host-seam <intention.json> --seal runs verify.command as installer.run_verify does and persists one VALIDATION through the store's door at intentions-not-beside-code/validations/<stem>/<host>.json, host = the box's short hostname lowercased; the record carries host facts (hostname, os-release ID and VERSION_ID, kernel) and the intention's fingerprint. standing(<host-seam intention>) reads only this box's file: proven while it is green, the facts still match and the intention is unchanged.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof; a host-seam had no way in) and Law 3 (the host-seam seal expires when the host drifts); outline 6.3.5 (verify, apply, re-verify).
answers.what: The tester runs a host-seam intention's verify.command and seals a validation for THIS box, so a host-seam crossing can name a proof that standing() reads as proven on the box that sealed it and on no other.

bullets.text: A host-seam seal is box-local by construction: a PROVED crossing for one means proven on the crossing box, and every other box reads not proven until it seals its own.
